title: Projectivity of finite graded algebras with finite degree zero
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}R_n$ a nonnegatively graded commutative $k$-algebra, with the structure map landing in $R_0$. Suppose $R$ is finitely generated over $k$ and $R_0$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. Then for every sufficiently divisible positive integer $d$, the Veronese algebra $R^{(d)}=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}R_{nd}$, regraded by $(R^{(d)})_n=R_{nd}$, is generated by its degree-one part over $R_0$, and there is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}R\simeq\operatorname{Proj}R^{(d)}$ [def-pc-proj]. The $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Proj}R$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and has a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_k$ for some finite $N\geq0$, hence is projective in [def-kun-projective]. The zero ring and the case $R_+=0$, when Proj is empty, are included; $R_0=k$ is not required.

source.place: Tag 0EGH, lemma-uple-generated-degree-1. Proj invariance: constructions.tex Tag 0B5J, lemma-d-uple; degree-one presentation: Tag 01N0, lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj. Projectivity over k uses the finite k-algebra R_0 and projective composition, morphisms.tex Tag 0C4P, lemma-composition-projective, and Tag 087S, lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective.

proof.text: Finite generation over k gives finite generation over R_0 by restriction of scalars. Apply the weighted-monomial theorem exists_veronese_generators, choosing a positive integer D all of whose multiples give degree-one generation.
For each positive d apply exists_veronese_proj_iso. Its explicit chart maps send a/s^q to the same fraction and the glued scheme isomorphism satisfies the required chart equation.

Mathlib ProjectiveSpectrum.Proper makes Proj R proper over Spec R_0. The map Spec R_0 to Spec k is finite because R_0 is finite dimensional. Their composite is proper and its source is compact. Apply exists_common_degree_twist_ample to the identity open immersion of Proj R, taking the first positive power to obtain an invertible ample module.

Apply IsAmple.exists_immersion_affine_base over k to that ample module, obtaining an immersion into a finite projective space. The immersion is closed: its composite to Spec k is universally closed, and projective space is separated over Spec k. Package it as IsHProjective. The existing instances then give local finite type and quasi-compactness.
